The season started on 21 January 2020 and ended on 31 December 2020. [[C.D. Jorge Wilstermann|Jorge Wilstermann]] were the defending champions, having won the [[2019 FBF División Profesional#Torneo Clausura|2019 Clausura]] tournament. [[Club Always Ready|Always Ready]] won their first title in the ''División Profesional'' and third overall (first since 1957) in the top flight of Bolivian football with a 2–0 victory over [[Nacional Potosí]] on the twenty-sixth and final matchday of the Torneo Apertura, played on 31 December. The tournament was suspended from 16 March to 27 November due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia|COVID-19 pandemic]]. As of 30 October 2020, Bolivia was the only one of [[CONMEBOL]]'s member associations to have its top-tier football league still suspended due to the pandemic.{{cite web|url=https://www.lostiempos.com/deportes/futbol/20201016/bolivia-es-unica-que-no-reinicia-su-torneo-nacional-futbol|title=Bolivia es la única que no reinicia su torneo nacional de fútbol|language=Spanish|publisher=Los Tiempos|date=16 October 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} ==Teams== The number of teams for the 2020 season remained the same as the previous season. [[Club Destroyers|Destroyers]] were relegated to the [[Copa Simón Bolívar]] after finishing in last place of the aggregate table in the [[2019 Bolivian Primera División season#Aggregate table|previous season]], with [[Sport Boys Warnes|Sport Boys]] being disaffiliated from the league after failing to show up for their last game of the season. Tiempos|date=17 December 2020|access-date=18 December 2020}} |} {{clear}} ==Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic== On 16 March, the [[Bolivian Football Federation]] (FBF) decided to suspend both the División Profesional and División Aficionados tournaments until 31 March due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia|COVID-19 pandemic]],{{cite web |url=https://deportetotal.com.bo/oficial-la-fbf-decidio-suspendio-el-torneo-hasta-el-31-de-marzo/|title=Oficial: La FBF suspendió el Torneo hasta el 31 de marzo|language=Spanish|publisher=Deporte Total|date=16 March 2020}} with the suspension being extended until the second semester of 2020 due to the extension of the lockdown and the ban on sporting activities until 31 May enacted by the Bolivian interim government.{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/es/noticias/no-habra-futbol-en-bolivia-en-mayo-ni-en-junio/10p8ouh3arzi912wp3uo3p9bhx|title=No habrá fútbol en Bolivia en mayo ni en junio|language=Spanish|publisher=Goal.com|date=29 April 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} On 2 June, the FBF presented to the Bolivian interim government a proposal to resume activities for both the [[Bolivia national football team|national team]] and the football league, with the national team starting training sessions from 15 June and the 14 División Profesional teams in July, resuming the tournament in August,{{cite web |url=https://es.besoccer.com/noticia/bolivia-pide-volver-en-agosto-842257|title=Bolivia pide volver en agosto|language=Spanish|publisher=BeSoccer|date=3 June 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} however, the government only approved the biosecurity protocols submitted by the FBF on 25 July, authorizing [[Club Bolívar|Bolívar]] and [[C.D. Jorge Wilstermann|Jorge Wilstermann]] to resume their training sessions on account of their involvement in the [[2020 Copa Libertadores]] which was scheduled to resume in September, while the other 12 División Profesional clubs had to submit their protocols to the Bolivian Society of Sports Medicine for their approval.{{cite web |url=https://www.americatv.com.pe/deportes/futbol-mundial/coronavirus-gobierno-boliviano-aprobo-protocolos-sanitarios-regreso-futbol-n405325|title=Coronavirus: Gobierno boliviano aprobó protocolos sanitarios para el regreso del fútbol|language=Spanish|publisher=América TV|date=25 July 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} On 5 June, in a virtual meeting of the Superior Council of the División Profesional, Bolívar's chairman [[Marcelo Claure]] proposed to resume and conclude the ''Torneo Apertura'' in [[Cochabamba]] over three weeks, a proposal backed by [[Club Aurora|Aurora]] and Jorge Wilstermann. In response to this proposal, FBF's Director of Competitions Adrián Monje stated that they would need seven stadiums for it to be implemented and the lack of places to train was a major limitation.{{cite web |url=https://www.paginasiete.bo/campeones/2020/6/5/claure-propone-una-sola-sede-cochabamba-para-terminar-el-apertura-257557.html|title=Claure propone una sola sede, Cochabamba, para terminar el Apertura|language=Spanish|publisher=Página Siete|date=5 June 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} On 12 August, the FBF presented a new proposal to resume the ''Torneo Apertura'' on 21 or 25 October, pending the development of the pandemic in the country,{{cite web |url=https://es.besoccer.com/noticia/la-federacion-boliviana-propuso-reanudar-el-futbol-en-octubre-872629|title=La Federación Boliviana propuso reanudar el fútbol en octubre|language=Spanish|publisher=BeSoccer|date=13 August 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} however, on 15 August the Ministry of Health through their General Manager of Hospitals René Sahonero stated that the Bolivian government was aiming at a resumption of the competition in the first week of November. Sahonero also stated that should the rates of COVID-19 infection failed to decrease by then, no tournament could be played for the remainder of the year.{{cite web |url=https://correodelsur.com/deporte/20200815_el-futbol-boliviano-podria-volver-a-las-canchas-en-noviembre.html|title=El fútbol boliviano podría volver a las canchas en noviembre|language=Spanish|publisher=Correo del Sur|date=15 August 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} On 8 September, the Bolivian government through its Vice-Minister of Sports Augusto Chávez stated that the Bolivian government would guarantee the return to activity of the División Profesional on the proposed deadlines of 21 or 25 October, as long as the 14 clubs of the league came to an agreement on a date for resumption, met biosecurity protocols, and matches were played behind closed doors. As of that day, six clubs had already resumed their training sessions: Bolívar, Jorge Wilstermann, [[Oriente Petrolero]], [[Club Blooming|Blooming]], [[Royal Pari F.C.|Royal Pari]], and [[Club Deportivo Guabirá|Guabirá]].{{cite web |url=https://www.la-razon.com/marcas/2020/09/08/el-gobierno-garantiza-el-retorno-del-futbol-local-entre-el-21-y-25-octubre/|title=El Gobierno garantiza el retorno del fútbol local entre el 21 y 25 octubre|language=Spanish|publisher=La Razón|date=8 September 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} However, on 8 October, FBF's Director of Competitions Adrián Monje stated that they had not yet received an official approval from the Bolivian central government to resume the competition, in spite of the fact that some local authorities were willing to grant their permission for matches to be played within their jurisdictions.{{cite web |url=https://www.lostiempos.com/deportes/futbol/20201008/fbf-aun-no-tiene-aval-del-estado-reinicio-del-torneo-apertura|title=Aún no hay fecha para el regreso del torneo Apertura de la División Profesional|language=Spanish|publisher=Los Tiempos|date=8 October 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} The death of FBF president [[César Salinas]] by COVID-19 on 19 July and the subsequent institutional crisis triggered by this event and the inability to come to an agreement on an interim president were also factors contributing to the delay in the resumption of the competition, as the 14 División Profesional clubs split into two groups backing different members of the FBF's Council as interims and failed to agree on a possible date of return to competition as both sides repeatedly boycotted and prevented the Superior Council of the División Profesional from taking place due to lack of quorum.{{cite web |url=https://www.lostiempos.com/deportes/futbol/20201018/futbol-nacional-crisis-dirigencial-puede-dejar-bolivia-futbol-esta|title=Fútbol nacional: crisis dirigencial puede dejar a Bolivia sin fútbol esta temporada|language=Spanish|publisher=Los Tiempos|date=18 October 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}}{{cite web |url=https://deportetotal.com.bo/lo-ideal-es-que-ninguno-de-los-dos-este-en-la-reunion/|title="Lo ideal es que ninguno de los dos esté en la reunión"|language=Spanish|publisher=Deporte Total|date=4 November 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} A Superior Council meeting scheduled for 5 November in [[La Paz]], called by both claimants to the FBF's interim presidency Marcos Rodríguez and Roberto Blanco, was cancelled by the former due to a civic strike which was also scheduled on that day in the city.{{cite web |url=https://deportetotal.com.bo/rodriguez-cancelo-el-consejo-superior-de-la-division-profesional/|title=Rodríguez canceló el Consejo Superior de la División Profesional|language=Spanish|publisher=Deporte Total|date=4 November 2020|access-date=6 November 2020}} On 11 November, it was revealed that the FBF was considering two proposals to return to competition: one of them was resuming the tournament on 22 November and ending on 13 January 2021, while the other one was resuming on 29 November and concluding the season on 23 January 2021, with the ''Torneo Apertura'' being the only competition to be played for the remainder of the season.{{cite web |url=http://eldeber.com.bo/futbol/hay-una-propuesta-de-reiniciar-el-campeonato-el-22-de-noviembre_208375|title=Hay una propuesta de reiniciar el campeonato el 22 de noviembre|language=Spanish|publisher=El Deber|date=11 November 2020}} That same day, Bolívar chairman Marcelo Claure announced that CONMEBOL would not accept any Bolivian entrants into the [[2021 Copa Libertadores]] or [[2021 Copa Sudamericana|Copa Sudamericana]] and the FBF would face sanctions in case league competition did not resume.{{cite web |url=http://eldeber.com.bo/futbol/la-postura-de-conmebol-si-no-vuelve-futbol-en-bolivia-no-habra-premios-y-se-sancionara_208369|title=La postura de Conmebol: Si no vuelve fútbol en Bolivia, no habrá premios y se sancionará|language=Spanish|publisher=El Deber|date=11 November 2020}} On 24 November, in a meeting of the Superior Council of the División Profesional held in La Paz, the representatives of the 14 clubs voted to resume the season starting from 28 November with the thirteenth matchday of the ''Torneo Apertura'' and ending on 31 December 2020 with the last matchday, meaning that 98 matches were to be played in 32 days. Furthermore, it was decided that no clubs would be relegated at the end of the season.{{cite web |url=https://deportetotal.com.bo/oficial-vuelve-el-futbol-boliviano/|title=OFICIAL: ¡Vuelve el fútbol boliviano!|language=Spanish|publisher=Deporte Total|date=24 November 2020}} ==Torneo Apertura== ===Standings=== {{#invoke:Sports table|main|style=WDL |update=complete
